edited_rows.rationale: The psalm opens with the imperative לְ֭כוּ נְרַנְּנָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.1, 'come, let us sing'), “Oh come, let’s sing to Yahweh.” (web:Ps.95.1), continuing in the same imperative-plural voice with נְקַדְּמָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.2, 'let us come before') through “Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving.” (web:Ps.95.2); the causal 'For' opening web:Ps.95.3 shifts from imperative summons to the grounds for it, closing this two-verse call to worship as one unit.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending this row through web:Ps.95.3 was rejected because that verse leaves the imperative-plural summons for a causal clause giving the grounds for worship.
observed_substrate_signals: oshb:Ps.95.1 and oshb:Ps.95.2 both open with imperative or cohortative-plural forms (לְ֭כוּ, נְקַדְּמָ֣ה), a pairing distinct from web:Ps.95.3's causal opener

edited_rows.rationale: web:Ps.95.3 opens with the causal כִּ֤י אֵ֣ל גָּד֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.95.3, 'for Yahweh is a great God'), giving the grounds for the preceding summons in a hymn of creation that names the deep places of the earth, the mountain heights (web:Ps.95.4), and “The sea is his, and he made it. His hands formed the dry land.” (web:Ps.95.5); the second imperative 'Oh come, let's worship' at web:Ps.95.6 opens a fresh summons, closing this three-verse causal unit.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: web:Ps.95.6 returns to the imperative register of vv.1-2 rather than continuing the causal, descriptive clauses of vv.3-5, so carrying this row through it was rejected.
observed_substrate_signals: כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.95.3, 'for') is the span's own causal opener, with no further כי-clause before web:Ps.95.6's return to the imperative
edited_rows.device_notes: The creation imagery (deep places, mountains, sea, dry land) is local to this span.

edited_rows.rationale: web:Ps.95.6 opens a second imperative summons, בֹּ֭אוּ נִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֣ה (oshb:Ps.95.6, 'come, let us bow down'), “Oh come, let’s worship and bow down.” (web:Ps.95.6), grounded in the covenant self-identification “We are the people of his pasture” (web:Ps.95.7); the verse then pivots on its own closing clause, “Today, oh that you would hear his voice!” (web:Ps.95.7), into the oath-oracle that follows at web:Ps.95.8, closing this two-verse summons-and-pivot unit before Yahweh's own first-person voice opens.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Folding web:Ps.95.7's closing clause into the following oracle span was rejected because the clause is still spoken by the worship leader urging the congregation to listen, not yet Yahweh's own first-person speech, which begins at web:Ps.95.8.
observed_substrate_signals: web:Ps.95.6 echoes web:Ps.95.1's opening imperative with a second, distinct verb of coming, pairing the two summonses that bracket the psalm's opening praise
edited_rows.device_notes: web:Ps.95.7's closing exhortation, “Today, oh that you would hear his voice!” (web:Ps.95.7), is the psalm's own lead-in to the oracle that follows.

edited_rows.rationale: web:Ps.95.8 opens “Don’t harden your heart,” (web:Ps.95.8), naming כִּמְרִיבָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.95.8, 'Meribah') and כְּי֥וֹם מַ֝סָּ֗ה (oshb:Ps.95.8, 'the day of Massah'); the first-person verb-suffixes נִ֭סּוּנִי and בְּ֝חָנ֗וּנִי (oshb:Ps.95.9, 'tested me', 'proved me') retroactively identify the speaker as Yahweh rather than the worship leader, so this rebuke belongs to the same oracle as “Forty long years” (web:Ps.95.10), naming אַרְבָּ֘עִ֤ים שָׁנָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.95.10, 'forty years'), and the closing oath, “Therefore I swore…” (web:Ps.95.11). The oracle runs to the psalm's closing verse, ending this four-verse unit.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Opening the oracle at web:Ps.95.9 alone, where the first-person object suffixes unambiguously mark Yahweh as speaker, was rejected because web:Ps.95.8's rebuke and web:Ps.95.9's account of the fathers' testing form one uninterrupted sentence in the Hebrew, with no intervening verb of speech to mark a new speaker mid-clause.
observed_substrate_signals: נִ֭סּוּנִי and בְּ֝חָנ֗וּנִי (oshb:Ps.95.9) carry first-person object suffixes (-ni, 'me'), marking Yahweh as the oracle's speaker
no Selah falls within this span; a paseq seg is disclosed at web:Ps.95.10 (single-witness; pmarks_Ps.json)
edited_rows.device_notes: The Meribah/Massah rebellion is named by spelling within this part: the prefixed spelling of Meribah occurs 1 verse book-wide (95:8); the bare name Meribah occurs 3 verses book-wide (81:8, 95:8, 106:32); the name Massah occurs 2 verses book-wide (6:7, 95:8) -- no comparable naming elsewhere within this part's span.

edited_rows.rationale: Psalm 96 stands as one liturgical composition; its rows group under one parent. The strophe opens with the doubled summons “Sing to Yahweh a new song! Sing to Yahweh, all the earth.” (web:Ps.96.1; byte: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ, oshb:Ps.96.1), widens through the missionary imperative “Declare his glory among the nations” (web:Ps.96.3), and turns causal at web:Ps.96.4 (“For Yahweh is great, and greatly to be praised!”), a grounding clause that runs through the sanctuary description closing web:Ps.96.6. A fresh vocative imperative cluster reopens the address at web:Ps.96.7 (“Ascribe to Yahweh, you families of nations”; byte: הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים, oshb:Ps.96.7), so the strophe boundary sits at 96:6|96:7.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Closing this unit at 96:3, right after the opening imperative burst, was rejected because the causal clause opening web:Ps.96.4 continues rather than answers that same summons.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ (oshb:Ps.96.1) opens the psalm with a doubled sing-imperative toward “all the earth” (web:Ps.96.1).
byte: הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים (oshb:Ps.96.7) reopens the vocative address to the nations' families, marking the strophe close at 96:6|96:7.
edited_rows.device_notes: “Sing to Yahweh a new song” (web:Ps.96.1; byte: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ, oshb:Ps.96.1) shares its first four Hebrew words, at skeleton tier, with the opening of web:Ps.98.1 (skeleton: שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ, oshb:Ps.98.1; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry this exact four-word new-song clause at skeleton tier -- 96:1, 98:1, and 149:1 -- of which only 96:1 falls inside this row's own span), though the two continuations diverge right after the shared clause: 96:1 repeats the sing-imperative toward “all the earth” (web:Ps.96.1) while 98:1 turns to a causal “for he has done marvelous things” (web:Ps.98.1).

edited_rows.rationale: The imperative cluster opened at web:Ps.96.7 runs through the worship call of web:Ps.96.9 (“Worship Yahweh in holy array. Tremble before him, all the earth.”), then the register shifts from imperative to declarative at web:Ps.96.10 with the embedded proclamation “Yahweh reigns.” (byte: אִמְר֤וּ בַגּוֹיִ֨ם יְה֘וָ֤ה מָלָ֗ךְ, oshb:Ps.96.10), and from there into the cosmic jussives of web:Ps.96.11-96.12 (“Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice.”) that resolve in the closing judgment formula of web:Ps.96.13 (“He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.”; byte: יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ, oshb:Ps.96.13).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Splitting off 96:10 alone as its own row was rejected: the kingship proclamation sits inside the same imperative-to-cosmic movement as 96:7-9 and 96:11-13, with no independent seam marker isolating it.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: אִמְר֤וּ בַגּוֹיִ֨ם יְה֘וָ֤ה מָלָ֗ךְ (oshb:Ps.96.10) carries the יהוה מלך kingship-proclamation clause embedded as reported speech inside 'say among the nations', one of two attested clause forms of this proclamation in this span; sweep of the יהוה מלך kingship formula: 1 verse inside this row's own span (96:10, within Ps.96.7-Ps.96.13), 6 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (10:16, 29:10, 93:1, 96:10, 97:1, 99:1) or 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (97:1, 99:1).
No selah occurs across this span (pmarks_Ps.json inventory; span-scoped absence).

edited_rows.rationale: All rows of this psalm belong to a single parent unit. The strophe opens with the standalone proclamation “Yahweh reigns! Let the earth rejoice! Let the multitude of islands be glad!” (web:Ps.97.1; byte: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ תָּגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ, oshb:Ps.97.1) and moves straight into theophany imagery — clouds, darkness, fire, and melting mountains — through web:Ps.97.2-97.5, closing this movement where the heavens themselves become witness at web:Ps.97.6 (“The heavens declare his righteousness.”). The address shifts at web:Ps.97.7 from cosmic description to a third-person/jussive form aimed at idol-worshippers (יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ, oshb:Ps.97.7, 'let them be shamed') alongside the verse's own true imperative, הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ ('worship him'), addressed to כָּל אֱלֹהִֽים (oshb:Ps.97.7, 'all you gods'), marking the strophe boundary at 97:6|97:7.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: A shorter opening ending at 97:4 was rejected because the mountain-melting image of web:Ps.97.5 completes rather than opens a new clause of the same theophany.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ תָּגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Ps.97.1) opens with the יהוה מלך clause as a verse-initial independent declaration; sweep of this exact verse-initial form: 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (97:1, 99:1), widening to 3 at accent_stripped tier (+93:1) and 4 at skeleton tier (+10:16, a noun-form homograph) -- only 97:1 falls inside this row's own span (Ps.97.1-Ps.97.6).

edited_rows.rationale: The strophe opens with a third-person/jussive form, “Let all them be shamed who serve engraved images” (web:Ps.97.7; byte: יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ כָּל עֹ֬בְדֵי פֶ֗סֶל, oshb:Ps.97.7), aimed at idol-worshippers -- the verse's own true imperative, הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ ('worship him'), is addressed instead to כָּל אֱלֹהִֽים ('all you gods') -- then follows Zion's glad response at web:Ps.97.8 (“Zion heard and was glad.”) into direct address to Yahweh at web:Ps.97.9 (“For you, Yahweh, are most high above all the earth.”). The address turns back to the congregation at web:Ps.97.10 with a fresh imperative, “You who love Yahweh, hate evil!”, running through the closing exhortation of web:Ps.97.12 (“Give thanks to his holy Name.”).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Treating 97:9 in isolation as its own row was considered and rejected because the direct address to Yahweh there answers rather than interrupts the idol-shame material opened at 97:7; the stronger rival is the fresh vocative-plus-imperative at 97:9|97:10, “You who love Yahweh, hate evil!” (web:Ps.97.10; byte: אֹהֲבֵ֥י יְהוָ֗ה שִׂנְא֫וּ, oshb:Ps.97.10), addressed to a new class (those who love Yahweh) rather than to Yahweh or the idol-worshippers; this rival seam remains unresolved, which the row's medium confidence reflects.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ כָּל עֹ֬בְדֵי פֶ֗סֶל (oshb:Ps.97.7) opens this unit's imperative addressed to idol-worshippers, distinct in addressee from the theophany description closing the prior strophe at 97:6.

edited_rows.rationale: The psalm coheres as one composition — parent grouping Psalm 98. Its title sits inside MT v1 (“A Psalm.”, web:Ps.98.0 = oshb:Ps.98.1; byte: מִזְמ֡וֹר), immediately followed by the new-song summons “Sing to Yahweh a new song” (web:Ps.98.1; byte: שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ, oshb:Ps.98.1) and its causal ground, “for he has done marvelous things!”. Third-person narration of Yahweh's acts runs through web:Ps.98.2-98.3, closing on “All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.” (web:Ps.98.3). A second, expanded imperative summons reopens at web:Ps.98.4 after this intervening third-person narrative, marking the strophe boundary at 98:3|98:4.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Folding 98:1-9 into one whole-psalm row was rejected: the narration of 98:1-3 and the imperative-plus-cosmic movement of 98:4-9 stay internally uniform in grammatical person, an independent tier-1 seam at 98:3|98:4.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: מִזְמ֡וֹר (oshb:Ps.98.1) stands as this title's genre-label word on its own; the superscription carries no second label word before the verse's own content begins.

byte: מִזְמ֡וֹר שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ (oshb:Ps.98.1) opens with the same four-word new-song clause as web:Ps.96.1, matching at skeleton tier (skeleton: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ, oshb:Ps.96.1); see the typed relation at web:Ps.96.1.

edited_rows.rationale: The imperative “Make a joyful noise to Yahweh, all the earth!” (web:Ps.98.4; byte: הָרִ֣יעוּ לַֽ֭יהוָה כָּל הָאָ֑רֶץ, oshb:Ps.98.4) opens a call to instrumental praise — harp, trumpet, and ram's horn — through web:Ps.98.6, then turns to third-person/jussive cosmic forms (sea, rivers, mountains) in web:Ps.98.7-98.8, closing on the judgment formula of web:Ps.98.9 (“He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.”; byte: יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים, oshb:Ps.98.9).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Claiming this closing formula matched web:Ps.96.13's closing formula word-for-word was rejected: collated at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses compared, 96:13 and 98:9) the two diverge (96:13 doubles “for he comes” (web:Ps.96.13) and closes on “his truth” (web:Ps.96.13) while 98:9 closes on “equity” (web:Ps.98.9), matching 96:10's own wording instead).
observed_substrate_signals: byte: לִֽפְֽנֵי יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (oshb:Ps.98.9) parallels but does not collate byte-identical to לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָ֨ה כִּ֬י בָ֗א כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.96.13) (collate: 2 verses compared); 98:9 lacks 96:13's doubled ‘for he comes’ and closes on a different final word.

edited_rows.rationale: One parent spans Psalm 99's rows. The strophe opens with the verse-initial proclamation “Yahweh reigns! Let the peoples tremble.” (web:Ps.99.1; byte: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ יִרְגְּז֣וּ עַמִּ֑ים, oshb:Ps.99.1), continues “Yahweh is great in Zion.” at web:Ps.99.2, and closes its opening movement on the refrain “He is Holy!” (web:Ps.99.3; byte: קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא, oshb:Ps.99.3).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 99:5 to gather both early refrain instances into one row was rejected: web:Ps.99.4 opens a distinct royal-justice clause in the third person (“The King's strength also loves justice.”) before turning to second-person address at its own second colon (“You establish equity.”; byte: אַ֭תָּה כּוֹנַ֣נְתָּ, oshb:Ps.99.4), an independent driver for a new strophe.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ יִרְגְּז֣וּ עַמִּ֑ים (oshb:Ps.99.1) opens with the same verse-initial יהוה מלך clause form as web:Ps.97.1; sweep of this qatal-verb form: 3 verses book-wide (93:1, 97:1, 99:1), of which only 99:1 falls in this row's own span. The wider skeleton-tier sweep catches 6 verses total; of the 3 excluded, 10:16 is the segolate noun מֶ֭לֶךְ (oshb:Ps.10.16), not this qatal verb, and web:Ps.96.10 carries the same qatal verb in a differently-formed, embedded clause rather than a verse-initial declaration.

edited_rows.rationale: The King's justice is named directly at web:Ps.99.4 (“The King’s strength also loves justice.”), a second-person address (“You establish equity.”) distinct from the third-person opening of the prior strophe. The imperative “Exalt Yahweh our God.” opens web:Ps.99.5 and the unit closes on the refrain's second instance, “He is Holy!” (web:Ps.99.5; byte: קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא, oshb:Ps.99.5), byte-identical to the refrain closing web:Ps.99.3 (collate: 2 verses match at byte tier, 99:3 and 99:5).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Merging 99:4 into the preceding strophe was rejected because its second-person address to Yahweh about royal justice has no antecedent vocative in 99:1-3; MT 99:3 does carry its own second-person element (שִׁ֭מְךָ, oshb:Ps.99.3, 'your name'), but the seam survives independently on the byte-identical refrain קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.3), which closes both 99:3 and 99:5.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.5) collates byte-identical to קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.3) (collate: 2 verses match), the same two-word refrain closing both verses.

edited_rows.rationale: The strophe turns from the psalmist's own heart to conduct among others: web:Ps.101.5 opens “I will silence whoever secretly slanders his neighbor.” (byte: מלושני מְלָשְׁנִ֬י בַסֵּ֨תֶר רֵעֵהוּ֮ אוֹת֪וֹ אַ֫צְמִ֥ית, oshb:Ps.101.5, ketiv/qere disclosed: ketiv מלושני plene / qere מְלָשְׁנִ֬י defective), naming those who will not dwell in his house through web:Ps.101.6-101.7 (“He who practices deceit won’t dwell within my house.”), and closes on the purge clause of web:Ps.101.8, “Morning by morning, I will destroy all the wicked of the land” (byte: לַבְּקָרִ֗ים אַצְמִ֥ית כָּל רִשְׁעֵי אָ֑רֶץ, oshb:Ps.101.8).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Treating 101:5 as the opening of a new psalm-level unit rather than a strophe within Psalm 101 was rejected: the parent grouping stated at web:Ps.101.0 = oshb:Ps.101.1 still governs every row of Psalm 101.
observed_substrate_signals: byte: מלושני מְלָשְׁנִ֬י (oshb:Ps.101.5) straddles a ketiv/qere spelling pair, the plene ketiv spelling set beside the pointed qere spelling -- disclosed per the kq inventory (pmarks_Ps.json); both spellings are the same word, the ketiv plene (with waw) against the qere defective (without waw).

edited_rows.rationale: The psalm opens on its superscription, “A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed and pours out his complaint before Yahweh.” (web:Ps.102.0), a tefillah (תְּ֭פִלָּה, oshb:Ps.102.1) title naming a genre rather than a person — tier-1 opener evidence. The double imperative plea that follows, “Hear my prayer, Yahweh! Let my cry come to you.” (web:Ps.102.1) and “Don’t hide your face from me in the day of my distress. Turn your ear to me. Answer me quickly in the day when I call.” (web:Ps.102.2), addresses Yahweh directly in the second person, and the reason-clause “For my days consume away like smoke. My bones are burned as a torch.” (web:Ps.102.3) closes the invocation just before the grass-bracketed complaint body opens at web:Ps.102.4.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Folding the whole individual-lament movement into one row was rejected because the grass inclusio marks a tighter unit that begins at web:Ps.102.4, leaving the vocative-imperative opening and its reason-clause (web:Ps.102.1-Ps.102.3) as the invocation proper.
observed_substrate_signals: title tefillah label תְּ֭פִלָּה (oshb:Ps.102.1) carries no name attribution; psalm_device_inventory.json's genre-label membership records tefillah at 5 psalms book-wide (17, 86, 90, 102, 142) against 0 name-label memberships for 102 in le_david (73 psalms), le_asaph (12 psalms), or livnei_qorach (11 psalms).
the row's imperative plea (web:Ps.102.1-Ps.102.2) addresses Yahweh in the second person, matching the psalm's title framing of a sufferer's direct complaint
edited_rows.device_notes: These rows resolve upward to Psalm 102 as parent. The tefillah title (web:Ps.102.0) and the psalm's own three-part movement — individual lament, Zion-restoration, and creation-permanence — shape the rows that follow.

edited_rows.rationale: This span is bracketed by the same simile word: “My heart is blighted like grass, and withered, for I forget to eat my bread.” (web:Ps.102.4), whose second word is כָ֭עֵשֶׂב (oshb:Ps.102.5), and “My days are like a long shadow. I have withered like grass.” (web:Ps.102.11), whose second-to-last word is כָּעֵ֥שֶׂב (oshb:Ps.102.12) — the same lexeme עשב bracketing the complaint body, skeleton-matching across the 2 verses (oshb:Ps.102.5, oshb:Ps.102.12). Between the brackets the row moves from bodily affliction (“By reason of the voice of my groaning, my bones stick to my skin.”, web:Ps.102.5) through the paired bird similes (“I am like a pelican of the wilderness. I have become as an owl of the waste places.”, web:Ps.102.6, and “I watch, and have become like a sparrow that is alone on the housetop.”, web:Ps.102.7) to the enemies' reproach (“My enemies reproach me all day. Those who are mad at me use my name as a curse.”, web:Ps.102.8), the ashes-for-bread image (web:Ps.102.9), and the second-person address returning at “because of your indignation and your wrath; for you have taken me up and thrown me away.” (web:Ps.102.10) before the shadow-and-grass close at web:Ps.102.11.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Splitting this span at the pelican/owl/sparrow simile pair (web:Ps.102.6-web:Ps.102.7) into two shorter rows was rejected because it would cut the grass-bracketed unit without any comparable seam signal inside it.
observed_substrate_signals: כָ֭עֵשֶׂב (web:Ps.102.4 = oshb:Ps.102.5) and כָּעֵ֥שֶׂב (web:Ps.102.11 = oshb:Ps.102.12) share the consonantal root עשב, bracketing the span
second-person address is absent across web:Ps.102.3-web:Ps.102.9 (seven verses) and returns at web:Ps.102.10, inside this row's own close
edited_rows.device_notes: This row is the individual-lament movement's body, framed by the grass inclusio (web:Ps.102.4, web:Ps.102.11) inside one row rather than split across the seam.

edited_rows.rationale: The row opens on the tier-1 adversative and addressee pivot, “But you, Yahweh, will remain forever; your renown endures to all generations.” (web:Ps.102.12), whose Hebrew opens וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.102.13) — a conjunctive vav plus the independent second-person pronoun אתה that readdresses Yahweh directly in the second person after web:Ps.102.3-web:Ps.102.9 (seven verses) run without it, the address returning briefly at web:Ps.102.10 before this row's own return at web:Ps.102.12. The turn opens the Zion oracle: “You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for it is time to have pity on her. Yes, the set time has come.” (web:Ps.102.13), the servants' pleasure “For your servants take pleasure in her stones, and have pity on her dust.” (web:Ps.102.14), the nations' fear of Yahweh's name (web:Ps.102.15), and the report “For Yahweh has built up Zion. He has appeared in his glory.” (web:Ps.102.16; byte: כִּֽי בָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה צִיּ֑וֹן נִ֝רְאָ֗ה בִּכְבוֹדֽוֹ, oshb:Ps.102.17), which opens an asyndetic completed-action chain that continues without a break through “He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.” (web:Ps.102.17; oshb:Ps.102.18); the genuine register break -- a new subject and the non-completed verb תִּכָּ֣תֶב (oshb:Ps.102.19) -- sits one verse later, at the seam 102:17|102:18, so this row closes on the rebuilding-and-response half of that chain.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending the row through web:Ps.102.22 as one continuous Zion-oracle block was rejected: the asyndetic completed-action chain opened at web:Ps.102.16 runs on, without a causal-particle break, through web:Ps.102.17; the row is closed here on topical grounds -- the rebuilding-and-response report -- while the chain's own grammatical break falls one verse later, at 102:17|102:18.
observed_substrate_signals: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה (web:Ps.102.12 = oshb:Ps.102.13) pairs the conjunctive vav with the independent pronoun אתה, a stronger contrastive marking than a bare vav
edited_rows.device_notes: The Zion-restoration movement (web:Ps.102.12-web:Ps.102.22) begins here; this row covers its rebuilding half.

edited_rows.rationale: The row opens with the closing member of the rebuilding-and-response chain begun at the seam 102:16|102:17, “He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.” (web:Ps.102.17; byte: פָּ֭נָה אֶל תְּפִלַּ֣ת הָעַרְעָ֑ר וְלֹֽא בָ֝זָ֗ה אֶת תְּפִלָּתָֽם, oshb:Ps.102.18), an asyndetic continuation with no causal particle of its own; the genuine register break -- a new subject ('this'/'a people') and the non-completed verb תִּכָּ֣תֶב (oshb:Ps.102.19) -- sits at this row's own next seam, 102:17|102:18, opening the forward-looking purpose clause “This will be written for the generation to come. A people which will be created will praise Yah,” (web:Ps.102.18); the sanctuary vantage “for he has looked down from the height of his sanctuary. From heaven, Yahweh saw the earth,” (web:Ps.102.19) opens onto the prisoner's release (web:Ps.102.20) and the proclamation “that men may declare Yahweh’s name in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem,” (web:Ps.102.21), closing on “when the peoples are gathered together, the kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.” (web:Ps.102.22).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Grouping web:Ps.102.17 with the preceding rebuilding report (web:Ps.102.12-web:Ps.102.16) was rejected because the purpose clause at web:Ps.102.18 opens a distinct forward-looking movement that this row keeps intact through its close at web:Ps.102.22.
observed_substrate_signals: the purpose clause at web:Ps.102.18 ('this will be written for the generation to come') marks a future-oriented register shift from the completed-action report closing web:Ps.102.16
edited_rows.device_notes: This row completes the Zion-restoration movement opened at web:Ps.102.12, closing on the nations gathered to serve Yahweh before web:Ps.102.23 returns to the psalmist's own voice.

edited_rows.rationale: The row returns abruptly to the psalmist's own voice, “He weakened my strength along the course. He shortened my days.” (web:Ps.102.23), reopening the first-person complaint that closed at web:Ps.102.11 and that the intervening Zion oracle (web:Ps.102.12-web:Ps.102.22) had set aside; MT web:Ps.102.23 (oshb:Ps.102.24) carries a ketiv כחו against a qere כֹּחִ֗י (pmarks_Ps.json kq), disclosed here though this row's boundary does not depend on either reading. The direct petition “I said, “My God, don’t take me away in the middle of my days. Your years are throughout all generations.” (web:Ps.102.24) turns at web:Ps.102.25 to creation theology, “Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands.” (byte: לְ֭פָנִים הָאָ֣רֶץ יָסַ֑דְתָּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ שָׁמָֽיִם, oshb:Ps.102.26), and closes on the contrast between what perishes and what endures, “They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a cloak, and they will be changed.” (web:Ps.102.26), “But you are the same. Your years will have no end.” (web:Ps.102.27), and the hope “The children of your servants will continue. Their offspring will be established before you.”” (web:Ps.102.28).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Reading web:Ps.102.23-web:Ps.102.24 as a continuation of the Zion oracle was rejected because the first-person pronouns reopen the psalmist's own complaint voice that the Zion oracle (web:Ps.102.12-web:Ps.102.22) had set aside; that oracle is third-person-only only across its stretch web:Ps.102.16-web:Ps.102.22 (MT 102:17-102:23, 7 verses), since its own opening verses (web:Ps.102.12-web:Ps.102.15) carry direct second-person address to Yahweh (וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה, oshb:Ps.102.13; אַתָּ֣ה, oshb:Ps.102.14; עֲ֭בָדֶיךָ, oshb:Ps.102.15; כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ, oshb:Ps.102.16).
observed_substrate_signals: MT oshb:Ps.102.24 carries a ketiv/qere pair כחו כֹּחִ֗י inside this row's span (web:Ps.102.23), matching pmarks_Ps.json's kq entry for this verse
edited_rows.device_notes: This row closes Psalm 102, moving from the psalmist's shortened days (web:Ps.102.23) through the earth's foundation (web:Ps.102.25) to the enduring servants' line (web:Ps.102.28).

edited_rows.rationale: The row's grammatical subject shifts from the summoned soul to Yahweh himself: “Yahweh executes righteous acts, and justice for all who are oppressed.” (web:Ps.103.6) opens with the participle עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת (oshb:Ps.103.6), moving from second-person imperative address (web:Ps.103.1-web:Ps.103.5) to third-person declaration; “He made known his ways to Moses, his deeds to the children of Israel.” (web:Ps.103.7) grounds the declaration historically before the row states Yahweh's own character, “Yahweh is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.” (web:Ps.103.8), and closes on the negated-accusation pair “He will not always accuse; neither will he stay angry forever.” (web:Ps.103.9) and “He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities.” (web:Ps.103.10).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Keeping web:Ps.103.6 with the preceding catalog (web:Ps.103.1-web:Ps.103.5) was rejected because the shift from second-person imperative address to third-person declaration about Yahweh marks a distinct discourse register.
observed_substrate_signals: עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת (oshb:Ps.103.6) is a participial third-person predicate, unlike the second-person imperative clause בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1)
edited_rows.device_notes: This row opens the chesed catalog's declarative half, restating in the third person what the second-person summons of web:Ps.103.1-web:Ps.103.5 addressed to the soul.

edited_rows.rationale: A three-verse correlative tricolon opens the row's second movement: “For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness toward those who fear him.” (web:Ps.103.11) — Hebrew כִּ֤י כִגְבֹ֣הַּ שָׁ֭מַיִם (oshb:Ps.103.11), where כִּ֤י is a plain causal/asseverative particle and the comparison itself is carried by the kaf-prefix on כִגְבֹ֣הַּ — continues through “As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.” (web:Ps.103.12) and “Like a father has compassion on his children, so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.” (web:Ps.103.13); the row then turns from simile to ground, “For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.” (web:Ps.103.14), whose own second כִּי (oshb:Ps.103.14, כִּי עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ) is complementizing, governed by זָ֝כ֗וּר ('he remembers that'), not causal -- the dust motif that hinges into the transience movement of web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.16.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Placing web:Ps.103.14 with the transience movement that follows (web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.16) was rejected because its verb still has Yahweh as subject, matching the compassion-simile chain rather than the new grammatical subject, man, that opens web:Ps.103.15.
observed_substrate_signals: כִּ֤י כִגְבֹ֣הַּ שָׁ֭מַיִם (oshb:Ps.103.11) opens with a causal/asseverative כִּ֤י -- the comparison itself is carried by the kaf-prefix on כִגְבֹ֣הַּ, not by כִּ֤י -- and כִּי עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ (oshb:Ps.103.14) repeats the particle in a complementizing use (governed by זָ֝כ֗וּר), neither instance a fresh simile marker
edited_rows.device_notes: The dust motif closing this row (web:Ps.103.14) hinges toward the grass-and-flower transience imagery of web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.16 without changing grammatical subject.

edited_rows.rationale: The subject changes to man at the row's opening, “As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.” (web:Ps.103.15), continued by the wind image “For the wind passes over it, and it is gone. Its place remembers it no more.” (web:Ps.103.16); the vav-initial clause “But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children,” (web:Ps.103.17), Hebrew וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.103.17, a construct chain in which Yahweh (יְהוָ֨ה) is the possessor / nomen rectum, and the vav-prefixed וְחֶ֤סֶד ('lovingkindness') is the grammatical subject) — a plainer conjunctive-vav contrast than the emphatic pronoun-plus-vav pivot at web:Ps.102.12, but still legible against the transience just described — turns from man's transience back to Yahweh's own loving kindness as subject and closes the row on the covenant-keepers of “to those who keep his covenant, to those who remember to obey his precepts.” (web:Ps.103.18).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ps.103.17's vav-clause as a return to the preceding compassion-simile row (web:Ps.103.11-web:Ps.103.14) was rejected because it answers the intervening transience description (web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.16), not the simile chain three verses earlier.
observed_substrate_signals: וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה (oshb:Ps.103.17) opens with a plain conjunctive vav on חסד, weaker than the vav-plus-pronoun construction וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה at oshb:Ps.102.13
edited_rows.device_notes: This row's transience-to-chesed pivot (web:Ps.103.15-web:Ps.103.17) parallels in shape, though not in Hebrew grammatical force, the adversative turn at web:Ps.102.12.

edited_rows.rationale: The row opens on the enthronement declaration “Yahweh has established his throne in the heavens. His kingdom rules over all.” (web:Ps.103.19), Hebrew יְֽהוָ֗ה בַּ֭שָּׁמַיִם הֵכִ֣ין (oshb:Ps.103.19), then widens the imperative ‘praise Yahweh’ from the soul addressed at web:Ps.103.1-web:Ps.103.2 outward to the angels, “Praise Yahweh, you angels of his, who are mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, obeying the voice of his word.” (web:Ps.103.20), Hebrew בָּרֲכ֥וּ יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.103.20) — a plural imperative, unlike the singular בָּרֲכִ֣י (oshb:Ps.103.1) addressed to the soul — then to his armies and his works (web:Ps.103.21-web:Ps.103.22) before the row's own closing clause, “Praise Yahweh, all you works of his, in all places of his dominion. Praise Yahweh, my soul!” (web:Ps.103.22), returns to the singular imperative and to the clause the psalm opened with. That closing clause, Hebrew בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ps.103.22), matches the opening clause בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.103.1) only at the skeleton tier across the 2 verses (oshb:Ps.103.1, oshb:Ps.103.22): 3 of the clause's 4 words differ across 4 accent codepoints (word 1 munah/merkha; word 2 dehi/geresh-muqdam+revia; word 4 etnachta/meteg), so the match is claimed at the skeleton tier, not the byte tier.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Reading web:Ps.103.22 as belonging with the cosmic-praise catalog of web:Ps.103.20-web:Ps.103.21 without separately flagging its closing clause was rejected because that clause repeats the psalm's own opening words and closes the inclusio opened at web:Ps.103.1.
observed_substrate_signals: בָּרֲכ֥וּ יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.103.20) is a plural imperative addressed to the angels, contrasting with the singular בָּרֲכִ֣י (oshb:Ps.103.1, oshb:Ps.103.22) addressed to the soul

the closing clause (oshb:Ps.103.22) matches the opening clause (oshb:Ps.103.1) at the skeleton tier across the 2 verses; 3 of 4 words differ across 4 accent codepoints (word 1 munah/merkha; word 2 dehi/geresh-muqdam+revia; word 4 etnachta/meteg)
edited_rows.device_notes: This row closes the barchi-nafshi inclusio opened at web:Ps.103.1, completing Psalm 103's parent grouping; the angelic call-to-bless (web:Ps.103.20-web:Ps.103.21) widens the summons before the closing return to my soul.

edited_rows.rationale: The psalm opens with the imperative inclusio that frames it, “Bless Yahweh, my soul” (web:Ps.104.1), with the Hebrew 'בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י' at oshb:Ps.104.1; the address then turns to second-person praise of Yahweh’s robing in light before shifting to third-person description of the heavens stretched “like a curtain” (web:Ps.104.2), the waters-roofed chambers and cloud-chariot (web:Ps.104.3), and the wind/fire messengers (web:Ps.104.4). This four-verse unit covers the robing-in-light and sky-building movement before the earth itself becomes the subject at 104:5.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through 104:5 (the earth’s foundation) was considered, but 104:5 introduces a new created object (the earth, not the heavens) under a new governing verb, marking a fresh movement rather than a continuation of the sky-building imagery.
observed_substrate_signals: imperative inclusio opener 'בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י' (oshb:Ps.104.1, tier: byte)
movement covers robing/light, heavens-as-curtain, water-chambers, cloud-chariot, wind/fire messengers (104:2-4)
the governing subject shifts from the heavens (104:2-4) to the earth (104:5), tier-1 topic seam
edited_rows.device_notes: Psalm 104 stands as one liturgical composition, spanning web:Ps.104.1 through web:Ps.104.35. The opening 'בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י' (oshb:Ps.104.1) recurs at the accent_stripped/skeleton tier at the psalm's own close (oshb:Ps.104.35) as its inclusio (byte tier differs: word 1 merkha at 104:1 vs munach at 104:35; word 2 revia at 104:1 vs dehi at 104:35); the identical phrase also frames the preceding psalm as its own opener and closer — sweep: 5 verses book-wide carry the skeleton 'ברכי נפשי', three of them outside this psalm — a typed cross-psalm relation (shared inclusio phrasing), never a merged row or shared authorship claim.

edited_rows.rationale: A new creative act opens the unit: “He laid the foundations of the earth” (web:Ps.104.5) — the Hebrew reads 'יָֽסַד אֶ֭רֶץ' (oshb:Ps.104.5) — governed by the verb 'יָֽסַד' (roughly 'founded') rather than the stretching/covering verbs of 104:2-4. The unit then narrates the primeval waters standing above the mountains (web:Ps.104.6), fleeing “At your rebuke” and “the voice of your thunder” (web:Ps.104.7), the mountains rising and valleys sinking (web:Ps.104.8), and closes on the fixed boundary set so the waters “may not pass over” and “don't turn again to cover the earth” (web:Ps.104.9).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Closing the unit at 104:8 and folding the boundary clause (104:9) into the following springs unit was considered, but 104:9’s “that they may not pass over” (web:Ps.104.9) completes the waters-in-retreat action begun at 104:6-7, not the springs-in-the-valleys topic that opens fresh at 104:10.
observed_substrate_signals: governing verb shifts from participial sky-building (104:2-4) to perfect 'יָֽסַד' 'founded' (104:5, oshb:Ps.104.5), tier-1 topic seam

second-person address to Yahweh (2ms suffix/verb forms: 'your rebuke' at 104:7, 'you set' at 104:9) runs alongside the primeval waters' own 3rd-person plural action sequence (flee, retreat, boundary-set) across 104:6-9

edited_rows.rationale: The topic turns from the sea’s retreat to fresh water given: “He sends springs into the valleys” (web:Ps.104.10), matching 'הַֽמְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ מַ֭עְיָנִים' at oshb:Ps.104.10 -- opening a water-provision sequence that runs as one topic through animals drinking at these springs (web:Ps.104.11), birds nesting and singing by them (web:Ps.104.12), and closes with Yahweh watering the mountains “from his rooms” so “The earth is filled with the fruit of your works” (web:Ps.104.13).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Running 104:10-13 together with the vegetation catalogue of 104:14-18 as one long unit was considered, but 104:14 opens with its own new participial verb ('מַצְמִ֤יחַ', roughly 'causing to sprout,' oshb:Ps.104.14) governing plant growth, a distinct topic from the springs/mountain-watering of 104:10-13.
observed_substrate_signals: the participial verb 'הַֽמְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ' opening the unit (104:10, oshb:Ps.104.10) shares its mem-preformative participial shape with 104:13 inside this row's own span, so it does not alone discriminate the seam
unit runs springs → animal drink → bird nesting → mountain-watering as one water-provision sequence

edited_rows.rationale: A second participial verb opens a new movement: “He causes the grass to grow” (web:Ps.104.14), whose Hebrew is 'מַצְמִ֤יחַ חָצִ֨יר' (oshb:Ps.104.14), governing vegetation rather than water. The catalogue runs through wine, oil, and bread “that strengthens man's heart” (web:Ps.104.15), the well-watered cedars of Lebanon “which he has planted” (web:Ps.104.16), nesting birds and the stork’s home in the cypress trees (web:Ps.104.17), and closes with the high mountains for wild goats and the rocks as “a refuge for the rock badgers” (web:Ps.104.18).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Splitting the human provisions (104:14-15) from the tree/animal habitat material (104:16-18) as two rows was considered, but neither stretch addresses anyone, and both develop the same unbroken habitat-and-provision topic opened by 'מַצְמִ֤יחַ' (oshb:Ps.104.14) -- even though 104:16 opens its own finite verb, יִ֭שְׂבְּעוּ (oshb:Ps.104.16), governing a new subject (the trees), rather than continuing 104:14's participle.
observed_substrate_signals: new participial verb 'מַצְמִ֤יחַ' opens the unit (104:14, oshb:Ps.104.14), tier-2 topic seam
catalogue moves from cultivated food (14-15) to wild trees and their animal residents (16-18) within one vegetation topic

edited_rows.rationale: A vocative-plus-exclamation in direct address opens the unit — a new rhetorical form, though not a new grammatical person, since second-person address to Yahweh is already continuous immediately before (104:20) and continues inside this row's own span (104:24, 104:26): “Yahweh, how many are your works!” (web:Ps.104.24), collated to 'מָֽה רַבּ֬וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֨יךָ יְֽהוָ֗ה' (oshb:Ps.104.24). “The earth is full of your riches” leads into the sea catalogue: “There is the sea, great and wide” (web:Ps.104.25), with ships and “leviathan, whom you formed to play there” (web:Ps.104.26), set against 'לִ֝וְיָתָ֗ן' (oshb:Ps.104.26).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Running 104:24-30 together as one providence unit was considered, but 104:27 opens with the collective pronoun 'כֻּ֭לָּם' (roughly 'the whole of them,' oshb:Ps.104.27) turning the address from the sea’s specific inhabitants to creation’s general dependence, a distinct referential class from the sea catalogue of 104:24-26.
observed_substrate_signals: direct-address vocative-plus-exclamation opens the unit (104:24); the grammatical person itself is unbroken (2ms address to Yahweh continues from 104:20 through 104:24 and 104:26), so the new element is the rhetorical form, not a shift from third-person description
sea catalogue (104:25-26) is a self-contained topic bounded by the exclamation before it and the collective-pronoun pickup after it
edited_rows.device_notes: WEB renders the sea creature at 104:26 as lowercase “leviathan” (byte-tier reading of the clean WEB text, not a title or proper-name capitalization); sweep: 2 verses book-wide carry the skeleton 'לויתן' (oshb:Ps.104.26), one other occurrence sitting outside this psalm.

edited_rows.rationale: The collective pronoun כֻּ֭לָּם opens this unit's clause, “These all wait for you” (web:Ps.104.27; oshb:Ps.104.27, כֻּ֭לָּם אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּר֑וּן) -- the identical pointed form כֻּ֭לָּם already occurs at 104:24, inside the preceding row's own span, referring there to Yahweh's works broadly; the recurrence does not itself mark the seam, since the 2nd-person addressee (Yahweh) is unbroken from 104:24 through this row's own close at 104:30. What changes at 104:27 is the 3rd-person referent -- from the sea's named inhabitants to creation's general dependence -- run through a sustained second-person cluster: “You give… You open your hand” (web:Ps.104.28), “You hide your face… You take away their breath” (web:Ps.104.29), plus “You send out your Spirit… You renew the face of the ground” (web:Ps.104.30), which closes the providence movement before the doxological response opens at 104:31.
